newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe bank rate cut, IMF aid boost shares.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe bank rate cut, IMF aid boost shares.

text.p: A further lowering this week of the central Reserve Bank's rediscount rate propelled the local bourse to new heights on Thursday, brokers said.
The key industrial share index soared 170.16 points -- a rise of 2.4 percent -- to close at an all time peak of 7,266.68.

"A further (small) cut in the rediscount rate to 27 percent by the Reserve Bank together with news that the IMF has agreed to support the second phase of the structural adjustment programme added impetus to the buying today," one broker said.

The Reserve Bank said on Wednesday it had eased, for the second time in two months, its rediscount rate by 0.5 percentage from 27.5 percent, citing declining annual inflation which is currently pegged at 20.6 percent from a peak of 28 percent at the beginning of the year.
It first lowered the benchmark rate at which it lends to financial institutions to 27.5 percent in August from 29.5 percent.

Commercial banks have also brought down their minimum lending rates with two of them slicing them to below 30 percent for the fist time in five years, a measure cautiously applauded by the country's private sector which has been complaining that the rates were choking growth.

Brokers said lower rates would benefit the stock market which is already reaping gains from investors deserting the money market where trading rates have fallen to the lower 20s from around 29 percent in January.

Finance Minister Herbert Murerwa also said on Wednesday the southern African country had won support from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) for a new economic reform programme due to be launched later this year.

Further Western donor aid for the plan was thrown into doubt last year after the IMF and the World Bank suspended some aid as its first reform programme drew to a close in 1995 after the government failed to meet some cost-saving measures.

On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Thursday, publishing group Zimpapers posted the day's biggest gains, suring 175 cents to 1,675, followed by 100-cent leaps in blue-chip conglomerate Delta to 3,300, cigarette manufacturer Rothmans to 3,500, bankers Barclays to 2,100, horticulture firm Ariston to 1,400.

Also among the winners, clothing retailer Truworths jumped 50 cents to 700, engineering group Gullivers rose 30 cents to 150 while winery Afdis and finance house Finhold put on 25 cents each to 450 and 925 respectively.

Minings were generally quiet with volumes spiked by large trades in Wankie Colliery involving external selling and buying which left it 10 cents higher at 360. Gold producer Falcon gained 100 cents to 1,600 while Falgold added five cents to 150.
The mining index crept up a marginal 1.46 points to 1,245.93.
